questions.question: A z-score of 0 means the value is...
questions.explanation: z = (x − mean) ÷ SD. If x equals the mean, the numerator is 0, so z = 0.

questions.question: What does a negative z-score tell you?
options: The value is below the mean
questions.explanation: A negative z-score only means the value sits below the mean. SD itself can never be negative.

questions.question: A score of 85 on a test with mean 70 and SD 10 has what z-score?
questions.explanation: z = (85 − 70) ÷ 10 = 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5. The score is 1.5 standard deviations above the mean.

questions.question: Maya scores 85 in Statistics (mean 70, SD 10) and 78 in Biology (mean 65, SD 6). In which subject did she do better relative to her class?
questions.explanation: Z-scores compare each score to its own class. Biology gives (78 − 65) ÷ 6 ≈ 2.17, beating Statistics' 1.5. The raw mark is not the right comparison.

questions.question: IQ has mean 100 and SD 15. What IQ corresponds to z = 2?
questions.explanation: Reverse the formula: x = μ + zσ = 100 + 2 × 15 = 130.

questions.question: When is it valid to say 'z = 1.5 means about the 93rd percentile'?
options: Only when the data are roughly bell-shaped (normal)
questions.explanation: The 93.3% comes from the normal distribution. For a strongly skewed dataset the z-score is still correct, but it does not map to that percentile.
